title: Answers to eikö possession questions with singular owners
summary: Answer negative possession questions about singular owners according to the stated fact.
prerequisiteSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
objectives: Answer negative possession questions about singular owners according to the stated fact.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Answer negative possession questions about singular owners according to the stated fact.
If the owner does have the thing, answer On. or Kyllä, on. If the owner does not have it, answer Ei ole. or Ei, ei ole. A negative question does not reverse the facts.
keyPoints: Answer negative possession questions about singular owners according to the stated fact.

examples.english: Don’t I have a ball? — I do have it.
steps: minulla means “I as the owner”. The question names palloa (“a ball”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.
Answer whether the person has the thing: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies it, even after a negative question.

examples.finnish: Eikö sinulla ole kirjaa? — Ei ole.
examples.english: Don’t you have a book? — You do not have it.
steps: sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person. The question names kirjaa (“a book”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.
Answer whether the person has the thing: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies it, even after a negative question.

examples.finnish: Eikö hänellä ole koiraa? — Kyllä, on.
examples.english: Doesn’t she have a dog? — She does have it.
steps: hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”. The question names koiraa (“a dog”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
Kyllä (“yes”) is an optional answer particle; On. alone also confirms possession.
Answer whether the person has the thing: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies it, even after a negative question.

examples.finnish: Eikö minulla ole kissaa? — Kyllä, on.
examples.english: Don’t I have a cat? — I do have it.
steps: minulla means “I as the owner”. The question names kissaa (“a cat”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
Kyllä (“yes”) is an optional answer particle; On. alone also confirms possession.
Answer whether the person has the thing: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies it, even after a negative question.

examples.finnish: Eikö hänellä ole peliä? — Ei, ei ole.
examples.english: Doesn’t he or she have a game? — No.
steps: Read the stated possession fact.
The owner does not have the thing: use ei ole.
The optional answer word does not change the fixed verb reply.

examples.finnish: Eikö hänellä ole autoa? — Ei ole.
examples.english: Doesn’t he or she have a car? — No.
steps: hänellä identifies the singular owner in this answers to eikö possession questions with singular owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
autoa (“a car”) is the complete regular singular partitive: auto + -a.
The stated fact denies possession, so reply Ei ole.

examples.finnish: Eikö minulla ole tyynyä? — Ei ole.
examples.english: Don’t I have a pillow? — No.
steps: minulla identifies the singular owner in this answers to eikö possession questions with singular owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
tyynyä (“a pillow”) is the complete regular singular partitive: tyyny + -ä.
The stated fact denies possession, so reply Ei ole.

examples.english: Don’t you have a pen? — Yes.
steps: Sinulla addresses one listener as owner.
kynää (“pen”) is the supplied complete singular partitive of kynä.
The fact confirms possession, so use fixed On.

commonMistakes: A negative question does not reverse the fact: On still confirms having the thing, and Ei ole still denies it.
Use the requested verb reply; optional Kyllä or an additional Ei does not replace on or ei ole.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Reply to “Eikö minulla ole kynää?” with “I do have it.” Use a verb reply; Kyllä or Ei is optional. kynä means “pen”.
practiceExercises.explanation: Answer the stated possession meaning: On confirms having it; Ei ole denies having it. Both remain fixed with every owner. An optional Kyllä or Ei can introduce the reply.

parts.formation: Kyllä means “yes”; it can introduce the affirmative verb reply.
Echo fixed on: the owner and thing are understood from the question.

answerDiagnostics.category: Negative possession question short answers: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Olen and en ole describe “I am” and “I am not”. A possession reply echoes fixed on or ei ole.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Complete the reply after “Eikö hänellä ole koiraa?”. The fact is “She does have a dog.”. Reply “Kyllä, ___.” Use koira (“dog”). Give the meaning “Yes.”
practiceExercises.explanation: The stated fact confirms possession. The reply uses fixed on, independently of the owner.
